description: TIMES-DK is a model listed in Open Energy Platform model and framework factsheets, a public register of energy-system model and framework factsheets under the section "Models", published or maintained by Technical University of Denmark (DTU), Danish Energy Agency. TIMES-DK is a multi-regional model, covering the entire Danish energy system. It is geographically aggregated to two regions, East (DKE) and West (DKW), with technological and economic projections until 2050. The model divided into 5 sectors namely: supply (SUP), power and heat (ELC), industry (IND), residential (RES), and transport (TRA). Coverage: not restricted to one place on the factsheet. Time resolution: annual, 32 time-slices in a year. Spatial resolution: national states, TSO regions, regions. Software: Interface software: VEDA-FE and VEDA-BE, Modelling language: GAMS, Solver: CPLEX. The listed link gives the source code or documentation; nothing was downloaded or run. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the factsheet. Caveats: this record was written from the Open Energy Platform factsheet only, so the code, documentation and any publication it links were not opened, their current availability was not checked, and the factsheet may lag the project. It can support energy-system planning and scenario studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-oep-factsheet-catalogue.

outputs: TIMES-DK is currently used in a multitude of roles at the Danish Energy Agency. The model is a part of the model suite used to make Denmark's Energy and Climate Outlook. It contributes to assessing the impacts of different energy policy changes in the medium to long term. Furthermore, it is capable of acting as a decision-making tool by providing insights into the dynamics of the different sectors of the Danish energy system models. Utilising the model for the creation of policy scenarios allows evaluating whether the energy system can reach desired targets and what set of measures are the most effective. Besides, can further be utilised for evaluating how uncertain parameters determine the possible future configurations of the energy system.
